set.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road to its parking lot. The Dune Wall is the huge buttress beside Angel Glacier on its right, at the foot of Mount Sorrow. The creek has to be crossed, and then a scree slope with small firs leads up to the base of the cliff. Hilti Hotel takes the obvious orange wall right of Stilgar's Corner.
set.descent_text: Lower from the anchor. A standard-length rope does not reach the ground, so a longer one is needed and care is needed while lowering.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts; descent stated on the route page or its own crag page.

set.approach: On the Icefields Parkway, a few hundred metres south of the Weeping Wall, a cluster of large boulders stands beside the road; park on the shoulder. The tall boulder with the bolted lines is a short walk from the road. New Pollution climbs straight up the biggest face on it, which faces west.

set.approach: From the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, take the trail that begins at the end of the pullout farthest from the outhouse. It skirts a pond and climbs a steep hill, then flattens and braids on its way up toward Hidden Valley. Continue to the ladder, climb it, keep to the main trail and bear left at any fork. First Wall is on the left a short walk beyond the ladder. Daisy Head Maisey is the second bolt line: it starts up a pinnacle and heads for the low slab section, then branches right at the top of the slab.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climbers' right, or rappel the route.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts; descent stated on the route page or its own crag page.

set.approach: From the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, follow the Hidden Valley trail past the ladder and First Wall. Beyond First Wall, follow the left-trending trail to a cleared area, which is Intermediate Slab. The slab gets plenty of sun and has top rope routes as well as sport lines.

set.approach: Park in the small roadside pullout with wooden signs for Roche Ronde and Smet, just before the bridge on Highway 16 near the east gate of the park. Cross the road to the blasted cliff face and take the obvious trail up its left side for a few steep metres, then bear onto the faint left branch where the trail first splits (easy to miss). The correct trail follows the crest of a grassy ridge with gentle drop-offs either side and occasional cairns; if the ground still slopes up on your left you are too low. Follow it up to a marked ridge, then up the ridge to a cairn between two small spruce trees, which marks the climbers' trail to the wall. A downward scramble protected by wire ropes comes shortly after, and the foot of the wall is a little beyond it, on your left, where the low first bolts are visible.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page plus the route page for where it starts.
